text:
Protection | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This document outlines the testing procedure P1, which must be performed on an 
annually bases as indicated by Y1 in the above title block
The type SFF31 relays are static under frequency relays that provide a single 
set point for under frequency tripping if the system disturbance such that the 
load excceds the generation the system is in danger of collapse, then this relay 
will trip the system. (Generator Protection)
The 
first draft initiated by eng. Fayza El-Sharkawy, tested by eng. Shirin Hamdy & 
eng. Azza Salama at 29 April 2003, revised by EDEPC quality control eng. Adel El-Nagar, accepted by 
general director eng. Mahmoud Saker and approved by eng. Moustfa Allam: Head Sector of Talkha Power Station.
Safety Precautions
A work 
 permit must be issued & the staff of test must be qualified and carry 
 the suitable safety precautions
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area is 
 required.
The generator must be out of service.
The generator must be out of service.

Work to be Carried Out
Preparation
Make Sure PT secondary circuit are opened at the 
incoming terminal blocks before isolating
the relay voltage circuit for test ,
Obtain copy of relay setting from field 
maintenance file and compare it with the setting on the relay.
Make Sure PT secondary circuit are opened at the 
incoming terminal blocks before isolating
the relay voltage circuit for test ,
Obtain copy of relay setting from field 
maintenance file and compare it with the setting on the relay.
Testing the Relay
Connect the relay studs ( 7 , 10 ) to the DC source 125 V DC where stud 
 7 is the + ve and stud 10 is the ve.
Connect the test leads between the trip contact ( 1 2 ).
Connect 
 test leads to line to line terminals ( 4 5 ).
Increase the voltage at 115 v.
Adjust 
 the frequency to a normal value.
Decrease the frequency slowly until the relay trips instantaneously.
Record 
 the frequency value and the time trip in the test sheet.
Return Relay and Associated Equipment to 
Service
Return relay to service by removing the 
 test leads from the relay terminal block and the test set i.e.
 - Disconnect the test leads from the terminals ( 4 - 5 )
 - Disconnect the test leads between the trip contact ( 1 - 2 ) 
 - Disconnect the DC terminals from ( 7-10 )
Make sure CT and PT secondary circuits 
 are in normal condition.
If any equipment associated with the 
 relay has been isolated, it should be returned to service by the following 
 restoration steps:
 - Breaker trip coils.
 - Breaker failure scheme associated this relay.
 - Disturbance alarm and fault recorder associated with this relay.
